assessment_scope: 0.1.0 reset baseline browser build: the six compiled DICE circuits (Pong, Pong Doubles, Space Race, Breakout, Stunt Cycle, Indy 4) with the portable chip-ROM adapter, compiled with Emscripten 3.1.74, and the legacy browser frontend still in place (controls/settings, player-supplied ROM loading through fflate, Home Screen manifest/icons and the qualification collector). Reviewed against the actual 0.1.0 build output, its notices and its corresponding-source archive. It covers browser JS/Wasm/asset distribution only; native binaries, toolchain containers, ROM payloads and the fifteen unported DICE circuits are excluded. It makes no gameplay, accuracy or browser-compatibility claim.

components.scope: NoCPU-maintained core adapters (core/), browser frontend (web/src, web/index.html), SVG icon and its derived PNGs, and the original DICE 0.9 sources compiled for the six circuits
components.license: GPL-3.0-only combined; NoCPU and DICE grants GPL-3.0-or-later individually
components.basis: tests/license-audit.json and docs/PROVENANCE.md; DICE sources are prepared unchanged from upstream/dice-0.9 (tests/source-manifest.json)

components.scope: Emscripten generated JavaScript (core/nocpu.js) and runtime support code
components.license: MIT option of MIT / NCSA dual license
components.basis: Installed compiler reports 3.1.74 (1092ec30a3fb1d46b1782ff1b4db5094d3d06ae5); retained LICENSE and AUTHORS are byte-identical to the installed SDK files; runtime source headers retained.

components.scope: LLVM libc++, libc++abi and compiler-rt members linked into the Wasm module
components.basis: Linker map: libc++ 12, libc++abi 10, compiler-rt 18 members. Retained LICENSE.TXT and CREDITS.TXT are byte-identical to the installed SDK files.

components.scope: musl libc members linked into the Wasm module, including 26 math routines
components.license: MIT for musl and the Arm-derived routines; the Sun-derived trigonometric routines keep their notice-preservation grant
components.basis: Linker map: libc 101 members. Math members: __cosdf, __fpclassifyl, __math_divzero, __math_invalid, __math_oflow, __math_uflow, __math_xflow, __rem_pio2_large, __rem_pio2f, __sindf, copysignl, cosf, exp, exp_data, fabsl, floor, fmod, fmodl, frexp, log, log_data, lroundf, roundf, scalbn, scalbnl, sinf — the same 26 as the reviewed legacy 0.6.0 inventory. Retained COPYRIGHT is byte-identical to the installed SDK file; the Sun and Arm headers are retained in docs/licenses/musl-emscripten-3.1.74-MATH-NOTICES.txt; the installed fmod.c (SHA-256 33fb61093e04783081b9e8f8a8a303456b2f919c215cd0c378c1ed0acf41934c) has no additional header.

components.scope: dlmalloc allocator and Emscripten support stubs linked into the Wasm module
components.license: CC0 / public-domain dedication for dlmalloc; Emscripten changes and stubs MIT
components.basis: Linker map: dlmalloc 2, noexit 1, stubs 1 members. Doug Lea's dedication and the Emscripten notices are retained.

components.scope: Vite modulepreload helper injected into the application bundle
components.basis: Installed vite 7.3.1; retained LICENSE.md is byte-identical to node_modules/vite/LICENSE.md.

components.scope: fflate ZIP deflate helper used by the local ROM-file validator
components.basis: The only npm runtime dependency in the frontend build provenance (node_modules/fflate/esm/browser.js); package, lockfile integrity and installed copy match the 0.8.2 pin checked by tools/package-web.py. Retained license is byte-identical to the installed package; unmodified preferred source (upstream/fflate-0.8.2) ships in the source archive; UZIP.js MIT attribution retained.

corresponding_source.delivery: tools/package-web.py builds the archive from the same checkout into the packaged site with its .sha256, links it from the app, and the release workflow attaches it as nocpu-0.1.0-source.tar.gz. It holds the unchanged DICE 0.9 sources, NoCPU core adapters and frontend, the fflate preferred source, the icon SVG and its rendering recipe, build scripts, lockfiles, manifests and all notices; it excludes Git metadata, ROMs, private fixtures, build output and compiled payloads.

review.by: Agent review of the actual local 0.1.0 build output on restart/desktop-first (commit 6994217).
findings: Shipped runtime: 11 files from build/web — index.html, assets/index-*.js (application with fflate and the Vite modulepreload helper), assets/core.worker-*.js, assets/index-*.css, core/nocpu.js (Emscripten glue), core/nocpu.wasm, icon.svg, three PNG icons and manifest.webmanifest. Local review runtime SHA-256 0d86c4b68782493aaac3b622ff1a7f7bddc4c3494b87a86b7604e04e1967c026; core/nocpu.wasm bc6f28066f194893c84a6ea0690a7fa9a39c06f32eb80eb6479b5426e80ce770; core/nocpu.js 623c8478e5669bfe254719c5b3ccb3fa58e2302b059d0b96283e32f81f99248a. Release packaging recomputes and records these in BUILD-MANIFEST.json.

Wasm link inventory (build/core/wasm/linker.map): 67 compiled NoCPU/DICE units plus seven SDK archive families with 145 members — libc 101, compiler-rt 18, libc++ 12, libc++abi 10, dlmalloc 2, noexit 1, stubs 1 — and the same 26 musl math members as the reviewed legacy 0.6.0 inventory. build/core/wasm/dependencies.mk lists only core/ and prepared DICE sources; no Qt, SDL, OpenGL, X11, ManyMouse, Phoenix, nall or zlib.

Core sources (core/, tools/prepare-core.py, tools/build-core.sh, upstream/) are unchanged since tag legacy-0.6.0 apart from core/README.md. Frontend changes since legacy-0.6.0 are NoCPU-owned (development-only ROM fixture loader, version fields); package.json and package-lock.json still pin one runtime dependency, fflate 0.8.2, and the build provenance records no other node_modules input.

Every retained toolchain notice (Emscripten LICENSE/AUTHORS, LLVM libc++/libc++abi/compiler-rt LICENSE and CREDITS, musl COPYRIGHT) is byte-identical to the installed Emscripten 3.1.74 SDK; the Vite and fflate licenses are byte-identical to the installed npm packages.
The packaged site carries all 27 notices listed here under notices/ with matching hashes, plus notices/browser-license-audit.json and source/nocpu-0.1.0-source.tar.gz with its .sha256.

The source archive (809 files) holds all 566 original DICE files, core/, web/ (including web/public/icon.svg and the derived PNGs), tools/ (including tools/render-icons.mjs), upstream/fflate-0.8.2, lockfiles, manifests and every notice; it has no Git metadata, build output, node_modules, compiled payloads or ROMs.

No fixture ROM member (29 members of the nine private fixture archives in build/roms) appears raw or base64-encoded in the web zip, the packaged site or the source archive; tests/test-dev-rom-exclusion.py passes on the production bundle with fixtures present.

independent_review.by: Independent agent (not the author of this assessment)
findings: Scratch clone of 6994217 with a simulated release commit and local v0.1.0 tag: build-core, build:web and package-web.py --tag v0.1.0 passed; runtime SHA-256 0d86c4b68782493aaac3b622ff1a7f7bddc4c3494b87a86b7604e04e1967c026 and core/nocpu.wasm bc6f28066f194893c84a6ea0690a7fa9a39c06f32eb80eb6479b5426e80ce770 match this record; the release workflow's checksum and notice/source guards passed.

Rebuilding the Wasm core and Vite output from the extracted source archive (no Git metadata) gave a byte-identical build/web. Caveat: that rebuild reused the already installed node_modules and Emscripten SDK (build/emsdk) rather than fetching them afresh.
Source archive: 809 files, equal to the tracked files at the tag plus RELEASE-MANIFEST.json.

Linker map members confirmed (libc 101, compiler-rt 18, libc++ 12, libc++abi 10, dlmalloc 2, noexit 1, stubs 1; 26 math members); Emscripten, LLVM, musl, Vite and fflate notices byte-identical to the installed copies; notice set unchanged from legacy-0.6.0 apart from the edited THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md.
ROM scan of the web zip, web tarball and source archive (including the source archive nested in the zip) for all nine fixture archives and their members, raw and base64 at three alignments: 0 hits.

excluded_components: Development-server ROM fixture plugin and web/src/dev-roms.ts (not in production output; tests/test-dev-rom-exclusion.py)
